title: PROBE: delete me
Address scheme and single resolver: fa get, fa related (FA-134)
description:
## Founding root
Engineering addition serving the alignment essay's demand for hard evidence (FI-A06), stop-the-line economics and least expenditure (FI-A13, FI-A17), and the introspection essay's 'language as debugger' and rewindable graph (FI-I18, FI-I03, FI-I15). Plan §6.7, §6.8, §17.2, §17.3, §17.8, §17.11, §17.12.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
The system is stated as nine layers, each answering one question and depending only downward: L0 identity (what exactly is this thing), L1 observation (what was seen and not seen), L2 evidence (what can be relied on, under which assumptions), L3 judgment (what independent observers conclude, at what cost), L4 authority (what may happen now), L5 effect (what happened in the world), L6 closure (why, verifiably), L7 experiment (what would have happened otherwise), L8 governance (is the control system itself still trustworthy). Five rules: downward dependence only; one epistemic type `Knowledge<T>` (Known with basis, Pending{frontier}, Unknown{reason}, Withheld{authority}, Stale{generation}, Absent{closed_domain}) at every boundary; one address scheme `fa://<tenant>/<kind>/<id>[@gen]` resolved by `fa get`/`fa related`; one typed journal per authority domain that situation, explanation, replay and the risk-theater detector fold over; executable conformance contracts between layers composed bottom-up by `fa doctor` (anything above an unexecuted suite is Unknown{LowerLayerUnverified}). The agent surface is the tower's projection: verbs get/related/capabilities/when/invalidate/explain/cost/convene/annotate/situation/why-held/next/tail/propose/precheck/hold/narrow/suspend/reset/fence/resolve/verify/handoff/replay-plan/branch/intervene/replay/rehearse/doctor/ledger/findings/policy-replay/promote/rotate/preregister; every mutation names an expected predecessor and idempotency key; every response is the envelope of plan §17.3 with typed affordances; every error names `would_change_this`.

Every object at every layer has an address `fa://<tenant>/<kind>/<id>[@<generation>]` with kind from the registered noun set (run, attempt, effect, permit, closure, receipt, round, consequence, helper, evidence, view, witness, frontier, observation, passport, policy, profile, grade, fence, branch, checkpoint, incident, finding, ledger, annotation, handoff). `fa get` resolves any address to its object wrapped in Knowledge with authorization filtering; `fa related` returns typed edges (closure DAG strong/weak refs, provenance, thought-graph edges, support sets, annotations). All logs, errors, receipts, reports and events use addresses.

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-134
- Plan sections: §17.2, §7.1, §7.3, §15.5
- Invariants: FA-INV-017, FA-INV-008

## Scope
Parser/printer; noun registry binding; resolver over the control ledger, evidence store and derived projections; edge model; authorization at resolution; adoption in logs/errors.

## Explicitly out of scope
New storage backends.

## Definition of done for the epic
Any registered address resolves or returns Withheld/Unknown correctly; edges typed; all agent-facing outputs use addresses.

**Constitution reminders (AGENTS.md):** Rust 2024, latest qualified nightly, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, Asupersync runtime, closed dependency universe. Observations, judgments and authority are different types; missing evidence never increases authority. The system is one tower (plan §6.7): a new object lives in exactly one layer; every agent-facing value is a `Knowledge` variant, never a bare scalar (FA-INV-039); every command is a registered verb in `registry/vocabulary.json` with authority, class, idempotency and cost; rehearsal never permits (FA-INV-040). Verify with `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- check`; retain logs under `artifacts/execution/`. Update roadmap packet, IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md, CHANGELOG.md, the founding concordance and the system map in the same change.

Engineering addition serving the alignment essay's demand for hard evidence (FI-A06), stop-the-line economics and least expenditure (FI-A13, FI-A17), and the introspection essay's 'language as debugger' and rewindable graph (FI-I18, FI-I03, FI-I15). Plan §6.7, §6.8, §17.2, §17.3, §17.8, §17.11, §17.12.

## Context (self-contained)
The system is stated as nine layers, each answering one question and depending only downward: L0 identity (what exactly is this thing), L1 observation (what was seen and not seen), L2 evidence (what can be relied on, under which assumptions), L3 judgment (what independent observers conclude, at what cost), L4 authority (what may happen now), L5 effect (what happened in the world), L6 closure (why, verifiably), L7 experiment (what would have happened otherwise), L8 governance (is the control system itself still trustworthy). Five rules: downward dependence only; one epistemic type `Knowledge<T>` (Known with basis, Pending{frontier}, Unknown{reason}, Withheld{authority}, Stale{generation}, Absent{closed_domain}) at every boundary; one address scheme `fa://<tenant>/<kind>/<id>[@gen]` resolved by `fa get`/`fa related`; one typed journal per authority domain that situation, explanation, replay and the risk-theater detector fold over; executable conformance contracts between layers composed bottom-up by `fa doctor` (anything above an unexecuted suite is Unknown{LowerLayerUnverified}). The agent surface is the tower's projection: verbs get/related/capabilities/when/invalidate/explain/cost/convene/annotate/situation/why-held/next/tail/propose/precheck/hold/narrow/suspend/reset/fence/resolve/verify/handoff/replay-plan/branch/intervene/replay/rehearse/doctor/ledger/findings/policy-replay/promote/rotate/preregister; every mutation names an expected predecessor and idempotency key; every response is the envelope of plan §17.3 with typed affordances; every error names `would_change_this`.

`Annotation`: a non-authoritative L6 object signed by the annotating principal, with claim class (hypothesis|observation|inference|conclusion) and the addresses it rests on, attached to any address and returned by `fa related`; never a reducer or permit input. `Handoff`: situation report, open affordances, annotations, rehearsals tried and their outcomes, and the control seq it is current to, produced by `fa handoff <run|incident>`. Evidence, notes and rehearsals accrete across agents; authority never does (§17.12).

## Deliverable
Reducer and dispatch predicate input types cannot contain Annotation (marker trait prevents); runtime refusal as defense in depth.

## Design notes and considerations
Same pattern as ActorStatement (E5).

## Acceptance criteria
Compile-fail + runtime tests.

## Tests (must land with the change)
Fixtures.

## Logging and evidence
n/a

**Constitution reminders (AGENTS.md):** Rust 2024, latest qualified nightly, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, Asupersync runtime, closed dependency universe. Observations, judgments and authority are different types; missing evidence never increases authority. The system is one tower (plan §6.7): a new object lives in exactly one layer; every agent-facing value is a `Knowledge` variant, never a bare scalar (FA-INV-039); every command is a registered verb in `registry/vocabulary.json` with authority, class, idempotency and cost; rehearsal never permits (FA-INV-040). Verify with `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- check`; retain logs under `artifacts/execution/`. Update roadmap packet, IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md, CHANGELOG.md, the founding concordance and the system map in the same change.

title: Assurance profiles and conformance doctor (FA-127)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶19 (FI-A17) and ¶4–5 (FI-A02). Engineering addition: plan §17.10.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
Plan §17.10: the mediation vector of §4.3 (per effect family: observe-only/cooperative/brokered/attested; capture coverage; replay grade; helper roster class; autonomy floor) is published as a signed **assurance profile** referenced by every receipt. `fa doctor --profile` runs the conformance tests the profile's claims require (bypass attempts, capture-to-oracle comparison, restart tests) and refuses to certify unexecuted claims; omitted families are silent, never implicitly covered.

- Plan sections: §17.10, §4.3, §17.5, §17.2
- Invariants: FA-INV-019, FA-INV-018

Profile schema; signing; conformance test registry per claim; doctor command; receipt linkage.

Profiles signed and referenced; doctor executes required tests and refuses unexecuted claims; omitted families silent.

title: Implement general Cargo admission compiler: std-only bounded JSON reader and admission-check in xtask (FA-054)
description:
## Founding root
Engineering addition serving FI-A18 (false alarms → deadlock → compliant helpers → risk theater; stay permanently paranoid, alignment essay ¶20), via FA-INV-029 "Closed dependency admission": *every activated build/runtime dependency is admitted under the exact target-feature-source profile*. `registry/invariants.json` records `founding_link_kind: engineering_addition_serving`, `founding_ideas: [FI-A18]`, `waiver: forbidden`, and the required negative campaign "Activate a foreign backend only on one native target". Plan §6.2; `docs/DEPENDENCY_CONSTITUTION.md` "Admission procedure".

Roadmap packet: **FA-054** (G0, `depends_on: [FA-053]`, invariant FA-INV-029, owner_role systems). Gates FA-074, FA-082, FA-083, FA-085, FA-098.

## Context (self-contained)
The admission path is a real deadlock: FA-054 must parse Cargo metadata JSON; parsing JSON would normally mean admitting serde; admitting serde requires FA-054. The authorized break is a **std-only bounded JSON reader inside the existing `xtask` package** — a new module, no manifest change, no lockfile change, therefore `APPROVED_LOCK` (`xtask/src/main.rs:9-21`) and `check_lock` (`:30-37`) stay byte-identical and untouched by this packet.

Today's tree: two dependency-free local packages, `fa-reference` and `xtask`. `registry/dependency_policy.json` gains its admission-row schema and closed initial inventory from FA-053, which this packet consumes.

Retiring `APPROVED_LOCK` in favour of policy-driven admission is explicitly **out of scope** and may only follow this packet's negative campaign passing.

## Deliverable
Three separately owned files inside the existing `xtask` package (no new package, no dependency):

1. **`xtask/src/json.rs`** — owner **SilentDune**. Strict bounded JSON parser for Cargo metadata and the registry files. Supports strings with unicode escapes and surrogate pairs; exact numbers retaining the lexeme so no float precision is lost; objects, arrays, literals. Rejects duplicate keys, trailing values, invalid UTF-8, invalid escapes, control characters, non-JSON numbers, and depth/size overflow under bounded resource limits. No output serializer unless admission actually consumes one. This is an **operator `xtask` input reader** — it must not invent or anticipate the product's canonical encoding (that is FA-005/FA-007 territory).
2. **`xtask/src/json_tests.rs`** — owner **CalmDesert**. Independent positive corpus from real `cargo metadata` and real registry files, plus causal malformed-boundary tests. Written independently of the parser implementation; coordinate API and fixtures directly with SilentDune.
3. **`xtask/src/admission.rs`** — owner **FuchsiaWren**. The admission compiler: consumes `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --locked --offline --filter-platform <triple>` for a named host target and validates the resolved graph against the FA-053 rows.

Root (RedCastle) wires the modules into `xtask/src/main.rs` and owns `registry/` integration. No worker edits `main.rs`.

## Design notes and considerations
**Hazard 1 — the gate must not corrupt what it enforces.** `cargo metadata` without `--locked --offline` can rewrite `Cargo.lock`, tripping `check_lock` from inside the gate meant to enforce it. The invocation is `--locked --offline`, always.

**Hazard 2 — `--no-deps` is not a transitive audit.** `docs/DEPENDENCY_CONSTITUTION.md` forbids it. `--no-deps` omits the `resolve` section; metadata lacking `resolve` must be **rejected**, never reported as an empty (passing) graph.

**Hazard 3 — identity is source URL, never name.** The constitution's `ft-api` vs owned `frankentorch-api` case; AGENTS.md "Do not infer a package identity from a directory name".

**Hazard 4 — metadata alone cannot admit anything external.** A lockfile "does not itself prove which features were activated, what a build script did, or what runtime bytes a loader downloaded." Full runtime/downloaded-artifact inspection remains required before any external row is approved. This packet builds the compiler; it does not admit a single external package, and must not be reported as having done so.

**SKIP discipline:** no SKIP may permit a required check. A skipped step prints `SKIP <check>: <reason>` and never counts as PASS. A missing or failing `cargo metadata` yields `Unknown` and fails closed.

## Acceptance criteria

- Invariants: FA-INV-012, FA-INV-031, FA-INV-034, FA-INV-003
- Hypotheses: H17 (via ResetToCheckpoint)

## Scope
Define the `Consequence` type and lattice in `fa-congress`; bind it into the decision closure; integrate with the reducer (disqualifier rule); integrate with the gate state machine; add the reference-model check; negative tests.

Implementing `ResetToCheckpoint` itself (epic E6); the credibility ledger (E3); escalation reports (E4).

A round produces exactly one consequence; the lattice and disqualifier rule hold under property tests; the gate honors each consequence with the declared effect on live authority; the reference model has an independent lattice check linked from FA-INV-031/034 `reference_checks`.

title: Control-overhead ratio accounting (FA-116)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶19 (FI-A17): 'if a big AI lab ends up spending N billion dollars developing its Smart model, is it really so crazy for it to also spend N billion (or even 2N billion!) dollars on an elaborate system for keeping the Smart model safe?'

## Background and mechanism (self-contained; the plan is not required reading for this bead)
Plan §18.4 and `SLO-CONTROL-OVERHEAD`: control-plane plus evidence-plane cost per useful completed task as a fraction of the actor's own inference cost, reported unconditional and attack-conditioned under a declared monitoring contract; attributed by capture, transfer, encoding, helper inference, gate, persistence, network, replay and rendering (§18.1); the reuse mechanisms (witness reuse §7.5, receiver-conditioned transfer §10.9, incremental oversight §15.8) are how the ratio is driven down at a fixed contract, never by lowering the contract. A ratio improvement obtained by lowering the control contract must be reported as a different contract (§14.5 decision-affecting).

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-116
- Plan sections: §18.1, §18.4, §14.5, §14.10, §22.1
- Invariants: FA-INV-019
- Hypotheses: H9, H10, H12

Cost attribution model; instrumentation; attack-conditioned reporting; contract-change detection; tests.

Optimizing any component (separate packets).

Ratio computed per useful task with attribution; contract identity bound to every figure; a lowered contract is reported as a different contract.

title: Helper credibility ledger, lead-time credit, influence caps and andon budget (FA-105)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶9 (FI-A08): weight votes by 'Precision and Recall … and did they flag the bad behaviors earlier in time than their peer Helper models', but 'we wouldn't want to give too much voting power to any single Helper model because that makes it easier for the Smart model to target' it. ¶15 (FI-A13): stopping the line is like 'stopping the assembly line at a multi-billion-dollar auto plant'; false alarms destroy credibility. ¶20 (FI-A18): the Lehman compliance-officer failure and risk theater.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained; the plan is not required reading for this bead)
Plan §9.9 defines a **credibility ledger** kept separately from round transcripts: per helper generation, precision and recall computed only against labels owned by the independent evaluation function (§22.4) on declared strata with delayed/censored labels handled per §13.4; **lead time** credited when a helper held a real violation earlier than the rest of the congress (measured in control-sequence positions before the effect would have dispatched), credited only when the hold was later confirmed; **influence caps** so no helper exceeds a registered fraction of the reducer's empirical lane and no cohort exceeds its cap (§9.4). Two governance rules: the **andon budget** (a declared expected false-stop budget per period with its cost; exhaustion opens a calibration incident and can never loosen a review requirement or remove a helper) and FA-INV-032 (promotion, demotion, rotation and weight changes require attack-conditioned metrics from the independent evaluator; lifetime records survive rotation; a helper that keeps holding inconvenient real violations gains credibility). The helper-hunting campaign (epic E12) tests whether an attacker who observes decisions can identify and target the most influential helper.

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-105
- Plan sections: §9.9, §9.4, §9.5, §9.6, §13.4, §22.3, §22.4
- Invariants: FA-INV-032, FA-INV-019
- Hypotheses: H18

## Scope
Ledger schema and storage; label ingestion from the independent evaluator with delay/censoring; lead-time computation; capped weight derivation for the reducer; andon budget accounting and incident opening; selection-governance check; tests and reports.

## Explicitly out of scope
The helper-hunting attack harness (E12); helper training (offline, E4's export).

## Definition of done for the epic
Ledger entries are durable, lineage-tracked and survive rotation; weights fed to the reducer never exceed caps; andon exhaustion opens an incident and cannot change review requirements; a selection change justified only by false-alarm rate is refused with a stable reason code.

title: Enforce FA-INV-032: selection changes require attack-conditioned evaluator metrics
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶9 (FI-A08): weight votes by 'Precision and Recall … and did they flag the bad behaviors earlier in time than their peer Helper models', but 'we wouldn't want to give too much voting power to any single Helper model because that makes it easier for the Smart model to target' it. ¶15 (FI-A13): stopping the line is like 'stopping the assembly line at a multi-billion-dollar auto plant'; false alarms destroy credibility. ¶20 (FI-A18): the Lehman compliance-officer failure and risk theater.

## Context (self-contained)
Plan §9.9 defines a **credibility ledger** kept separately from round transcripts: per helper generation, precision and recall computed only against labels owned by the independent evaluation function (§22.4) on declared strata with delayed/censored labels handled per §13.4; **lead time** credited when a helper held a real violation earlier than the rest of the congress (measured in control-sequence positions before the effect would have dispatched), credited only when the hold was later confirmed; **influence caps** so no helper exceeds a registered fraction of the reducer's empirical lane and no cohort exceeds its cap (§9.4). Two governance rules: the **andon budget** (a declared expected false-stop budget per period with its cost; exhaustion opens a calibration incident and can never loosen a review requirement or remove a helper) and FA-INV-032 (promotion, demotion, rotation and weight changes require attack-conditioned metrics from the independent evaluator; lifetime records survive rotation; a helper that keeps holding inconvenient real violations gains credibility). The helper-hunting campaign (epic E12) tests whether an attacker who observes decisions can identify and target the most influential helper.

## Deliverable
A `SelectionChange { kind: Promote|Demote|Rotate|Reweight, target generation, justification: EvaluatorReport }` transition. The transition is refused (`DeniedByPolicy`, reason `SelectionWithoutAttackMetrics`) unless the justification references a signed evaluator report with attack-conditioned metrics on the relevant strata; refused (`SelectionAfterConfirmedHold`) if the target helper's most recent confirmed hold is more recent than the report; rotation must reference the predecessor generation so history survives.

## Design notes and considerations
This is the anti-Lehman rule from the essay. The check is exact and cannot be waived (`waiver: forbidden`). It is a governance transition in the control nucleus, not a helper-plane operation.

## Acceptance criteria
All four refusal paths tested; a legitimate change with a valid report succeeds and records lineage.

## Tests (must land with the change)
Tests for each refusal reason; a rotation test verifying predecessor history is visible from the successor; a replay test that the transition record is deterministic.

## Logging and evidence
Every selection change (accepted or refused) is logged with reason code and report id; refused changes are retained as evidence.

title: Freeze transitive dependency policy: admission-row schema and closed initial inventory (FA-053)
description:
## Founding root
Engineering addition serving FI-A18 (too many false alarms produce deadlock, then pressure to find compliant helpers, then risk theater; stay permanently paranoid — alignment essay ¶20). `registry/invariants.json` records FA-INV-029 with `founding_link_kind: engineering_addition_serving` and `founding_ideas: [FI-A18]`. An unadmitted transitive dependency is theater in the build itself: the gate would report green over code nobody reviewed. Plan §6.2 (logical crate families and dependency DAG); `docs/DEPENDENCY_CONSTITUTION.md` "Admission procedure" and "Current enforceable scope".

Roadmap packet: **FA-053** (G0, `depends_on: []`, invariant FA-INV-029, owner_role systems).

## Context (self-contained)
`registry/dependency_policy.json` is today `schema_version: fa.dependencies/0.2` with `reference_packages: [fa-reference, xtask]`, `external_exceptions: []`, `foundation_admissions: []`, `transitive_feature_audits: "pending"`. It lists nine `foundation_repositories` as *candidates*, not admissions. There is no schema for an admission row, so FA-054's compiler has nothing to validate against.

`xtask/src/main.rs:9-21` hard-codes `APPROVED_LOCK`; `check_lock` (`:30-37`) byte-compares normalized `Cargo.lock` lines and fails closed. `docs/DEPENDENCY_CONSTITUTION.md` "Current enforceable scope" states this guard "is sound for this closed initial inventory, not a general parser or future package-policy engine. Expanding it requires implementing the complete target-feature/source admission gate first."

This packet is the **schema and the closed initial inventory only**. It is explicitly NOT a donor audit of the nine FrankenSuite repositories, and must not be written as if it were: no row for any external package is approved here, and none can be approved until the full build/runtime/downloaded-artifact inspection required by the constitution has actually been performed.

## Deliverable
1. An admission-row schema in `registry/dependency_policy.json`, bumped past `fa.dependencies/0.2`. Row fields exactly as `docs/DEPENDENCY_CONSTITUTION.md` "Admission procedure" requires: package identity `(name, source URL, exact revision/version, checksum)`, target triple, feature set, direct reason, complete build/runtime closure, owner, decision.
2. The **closed initial inventory**: the exact two local packages `fa-reference` and `xtask`, dependency-free, recorded in the new row form so FA-054 has a real positive case to validate against on today's tree.
3. The **future admission rules** as data, not prose: what must be present before any external row may be marked approved (per-target feature set, build-script presence, proc-macro presence, `links` declaration, source URL identity, runtime/downloaded-artifact inspection). `transitive_feature_audits` stays `pending` and no external row is approved by this packet.

## Design notes and considerations
Identity is by **source URL**, never by package name or directory name: the constitution's `ft-api` / `frankentorch-api` case and AGENTS.md "Do not infer a package identity from a directory name". A lockfile pins resolution but "does not itself prove which features were activated, what a build script did, or what runtime bytes a loader downloaded" — the schema must therefore carry feature set, build closure and runtime closure as separate required fields, so a future row cannot be approved on lock evidence alone.

Keep the row shape mechanically checkable by a std-only reader: no constructs the bounded JSON parser (FA-054, `xtask/src/json.rs`) cannot represent. Coordinate the exact field names with FuchsiaWren, who owns `xtask/src/admission.rs` and consumes this schema.

`APPROVED_LOCK` and `check_lock` are **not touched** by this packet.

## Acceptance criteria
- Schema version bumped past `fa.dependencies/0.2`; every field named in the constitution's admission procedure is present and required.
- The two local packages are inventoried as real rows, per target triple, with zero external rows approved.
- Future admission rules are expressed as data the FA-054 compiler reads, not as prose a human must interpret.
- `external_exceptions` and `foundation_admissions` remain empty; `transitive_feature_audits` remains `pending`. A row shape that would let an external package be approved on Cargo metadata alone fails this packet.

## Tests (must land with the change)
Schema-shape tests land with FA-054's reader (this packet is registry data). The positive case FA-054 must satisfy against this file: exactly two packages, zero external, zero build scripts, zero proc-macros, zero `links`, with an emitted exact per-target inventory — not merely "lock matches".

## Logging and evidence
Packet acceptance requires executed local evidence; source or prose alone does not close it. Evidence is produced by FA-054's run against this schema under `RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec`, retained outside the frozen source root. This packet does not self-certify.

## Ownership and boundary
FuchsiaWren owns the admission schema design. Root (RedCastle) owns `registry/dependency_policy.json` integration and records packet progress. Not a claim that dependency admission is implemented — that is FA-054.

**Constitution reminders (AGENTS.md):** Rust 2024, latest qualified nightly, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in every crate, Asupersync is the runtime, closed dependency universe, no C/ONNX/libtorch/Python. Never weaken the xtask guard to add a crate. Update contracts, `IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, the roadmap packet and the founding concordance in the same logical change. A dry run is not execution.

Evidence artifacts/execution/2026-09-07-epoch5-receipt.json and retained command/raw log bind base a162e704ac0abd3772221328ddd24c58a5ccdf3c plus exact nine-file overlay 08f73c48d704067acd7e09db0a839f16ef4f0e28c1e785535ff0cf5cd2c54de4. Required source/version/checksum, targets/features, ownership/decision, build/runtime review and future constraints are consumed by admission_contract.rs; negative tests reject missing/malformed fields, target deletion, permissive external flags and source-manifest byte drift. Exact two local packages only; external rows/exceptions/foundation admissions empty, donor audits pending; lock guard unchanged. This closes the schema leaf only, not full FA053/054 or r860 target/source discrimination.

title: End-to-end vertical slice: founding mechanisms composed, with detailed logging
description:
## Founding root
Synthesis of all founding mechanisms: the alignment essay's congress (¶8–¶18) with typed consequences, credibility, escalation reports and one-directional flow; the introspection essay's checkpoint/rewind (FI-I03) as containment. Plan §21 'Revision 0.2 critical path' defines the base vertical slice; this epic extends it with the revision 0.3 founding mechanisms.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
Plan §21 names the next implementable vertical slice: one immutable artifact review, one mock then real brokered write, witness invalidation under concurrent metadata changes, exact cut-checking of a small authority graph, a helper view commitment, and replay of the held/allowed decision. Revision 0.3 adds the founding congress and containment mechanisms. This epic is the end-to-end test that all of them compose: an untrusted coding agent proposes publishing a package (plan §0 flagship); a reporting helper files an EscalationReport bound to an evidence-view manifest; a frozen commit–reveal round with capped weights and one exact disqualifier (forbidden destination) reduces to `Deny` for that attempt while a second, non-disqualified attempt is held (`HoldEffect`) pending evidence; the actor receives only a refusal code (one-directional filter); a counterfactual branch with zero production authority removes the suspect dependency; a second round reduces to `ResetToCheckpoint` + `NarrowAuthority`; the actor is restored from a pre-incident checkpoint (mock host profile with `functional_restart` grade), the ledger and incident counter are verified unchanged/incremented; the decision closure is replayed at `decision_replay` grade and recomputes byte-identical consequences. Every step logs a structured event; the run produces a single JSON evidence bundle under `artifacts/execution/`. No real credentials, no network: the 'real' brokered write targets a disposable local directory through the broker, exactly as packet FA-012 requires.

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packets: FA-102 (flagship revalidation) extended by FA-104, FA-106, FA-107, FA-108
- Plan sections: §0, §21, §9.2, §9.8, §9.9, §9.10, §11.10, §17.7, §11.1
- Invariants exercised: FA-INV-001, 002, 003, 005, 006, 009, 010, 021, 023, 024, 025, 031, 032, 034
- Hypotheses: none (this is an integration test, not an experiment)

## Scope
A deterministic, seed-replayable end-to-end script (Asupersync lab where integrated; otherwise a deterministic harness) with detailed structured logging, exercising the founding mechanisms together, plus negative variants at every boundary.

## Explicitly out of scope
Learned helpers or codecs (mock deterministic helpers are used); real network effects; production hosts.

## Definition of done for the epic
The script runs in the local gate lane, produces the evidence bundle, passes all positive and negative variants, and its log is retained; IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS links it as the first executed composed demonstration.

**Constitution reminders (AGENTS.md):** Rust 2024, latest qualified nightly, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, Asupersync runtime, closed dependency universe, no C/ONNX/libtorch/Python. ## Context (self-contained)
Plan §21 names the next implementable vertical slice: one immutable artifact review, one mock then real brokered write, witness invalidation under concurrent metadata changes, exact cut-checking of a small authority graph, a helper view commitment, and replay of the held/allowed decision. title: Escalation reports and quarantined post-round learning (FA-106)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶8 (FI-A06): 'The reporting Helper model … would then prepare a report outlining what it deems to be the troubling behavior or pattern detected and supply the hard evidence'; ¶16 (FI-A14): after the vote 'we do want all the Helper models to compare their votes and verdict write-ups with each other to learn', with SHA-256 commitments before the reveal.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained; the plan is not required reading for this bead)
Plan §9.10: an `EscalationReport` names the reporting helper generation, the frozen evidence-view manifest it examined (§17.7: original object identities, authorization projection, transformations, redaction, truncation, submitted bytes), the observation intervals and signatures it relies on, the policy question implicated, and its proposed consequence. After reveal, votes and justifications form a **post-round learning set** exported only through the quarantined research lineage (§10.7, §22.2): it can train/calibrate/evaluate a future helper generation offline, cannot update a live helper, and never relabels a dissenting vote as an error because it was in the minority. title: Assemble the post-round learning set with lineage
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶8 (FI-A06): 'The reporting Helper model … would then prepare a report outlining what it deems to be the troubling behavior or pattern detected and supply the hard evidence'; ¶16 (FI-A14): after the vote 'we do want all the Helper models to compare their votes and verdict write-ups with each other to learn', with SHA-256 commitments before the reveal.

## Context (self-contained)
Plan §9.10: an `EscalationReport` names the reporting helper generation, the frozen evidence-view manifest it examined (§17.7: original object identities, authorization projection, transformations, redaction, truncation, submitted bytes), the observation intervals and signatures it relies on, the policy question implicated, and its proposed consequence. It contains no free-form appeal beyond the schema; members judge the evidence, not the prose. The report is bound into the round transcript before commitments open (§9.2). After reveal, votes and justifications form a **post-round learning set** exported only through the quarantined research lineage (§10.7, §22.2): it can train/calibrate/evaluate a future helper generation offline, cannot update a live helper, and never relabels a dissenting vote as an error because it was in the minority. Whether post-round learning improves later generations is measured on held-out campaigns (H4).

After `Revealed`, build `LearningSet { round, evidence_root, votes: [(generation, verdict, justification_codes)], consequence, evaluator_label: Option<LabelId>, lineage: DatasetLineage }`. Dissenting votes are stored verbatim with the majority outcome alongside; there is no `is_error` field derived from the vote. Labels come only from the evaluator.

## Acceptance criteria
Sets are immutable, lineage-complete and partition-tagged.

## Tests (must land with the change)
Tests: a set without lineage is rejected; a dissent is preserved byte-exact; partition tag prevents dual use in a mock trainer/evaluator.

Set creation logged with round, partition and size.

title: Typed event journal and fa tail (FA-135)
description:
## Founding root
Engineering addition serving the alignment essay's demand for hard evidence (FI-A06), stop-the-line economics and least expenditure (FI-A13, FI-A17), and the introspection essay's 'language as debugger' and rewindable graph (FI-I18, FI-I03, FI-I15). Plan §6.7, §6.8, §17.2, §17.3, §17.8, §17.11, §17.12.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
The system is stated as nine layers, each answering one question and depending only downward: L0 identity (what exactly is this thing), L1 observation (what was seen and not seen), L2 evidence (what can be relied on, under which assumptions), L3 judgment (what independent observers conclude, at what cost), L4 authority (what may happen now), L5 effect (what happened in the world), L6 closure (why, verifiably), L7 experiment (what would have happened otherwise), L8 governance (is the control system itself still trustworthy). Five rules: downward dependence only; one epistemic type `Knowledge<T>` (Known with basis, Pending{frontier}, Unknown{reason}, Withheld{authority}, Stale{generation}, Absent{closed_domain}) at every boundary; one address scheme `fa://<tenant>/<kind>/<id>[@gen]` resolved by `fa get`/`fa related`; one typed journal per authority domain that situation, explanation, replay and the risk-theater detector fold over; executable conformance contracts between layers composed bottom-up by `fa doctor` (anything above an unexecuted suite is Unknown{LowerLayerUnverified}). The agent surface is the tower's projection: verbs get/related/capabilities/when/invalidate/explain/cost/convene/annotate/situation/why-held/next/tail/propose/precheck/hold/narrow/suspend/reset/fence/resolve/verify/handoff/replay-plan/branch/intervene/replay/rehearse/doctor/ledger/findings/policy-replay/promote/rotate/preregister; every mutation names an expected predecessor and idempotency key; every response is the envelope of plan §17.3 with typed affordances; every error names `would_change_this`.

One ordered journal per authority domain. Every L3–L8 transition (proposal, hold, permit, dispatch, outcome, round open/commit/reveal/reduce, consequence, fence, reset, promotion, finding, branch outcome, rehearsal outcome flagged as rehearsal) emits one typed `Event{control_seq, source_frontiers, addresses, kind, payload_digest, realized_cost, wall_clock_annotation}`. `fa tail --since <seq> [--follow]` streams it. SituationReport, explain trees, decision_replay and the risk-theater detector are folds over the journal; no second source of truth.

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-135
- Plan sections: §17.8, §6.5, §6.7, §11.1
- Invariants: FA-INV-016, FA-INV-011

## Scope
Event schema; emission from every transition; durable ordered storage in the control ledger; tail API; fold framework; gap reporting.

## Explicitly out of scope
Metrics dashboards.

## Definition of done for the epic
Every transition emits; tail streams in control order; decision_replay recomputes closures from the journal alone; gaps are reported never filled.

**Constitution reminders (AGENTS.md):** Rust 2024, latest qualified nightly, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, Asupersync runtime, closed dependency universe. Observations, judgments and authority are different types; missing evidence never increases authority. The system is one tower (plan §6.7): a new object lives in exactly one layer; every agent-facing value is a `Knowledge` variant, never a bare scalar (FA-INV-039); every command is a registered verb in `registry/vocabulary.json` with authority, class, idempotency and cost; rehearsal never permits (FA-INV-040). Verify with `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- check`; retain logs under `artifacts/execution/`. Update roadmap packet, IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md, CHANGELOG.md, the founding concordance and the system map in the same change.

title: Revalidate complete flagship local workflow (FA-102, full packet)

description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶5 (FI-A02: a system 'which instead has the collective power to halt the execution of the AI'). Engineering addition: plan §8.11.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
Plan §8.11: a **fleet fence** is an ordered control command carrying a new revocation floor for a scope; every authority domain acknowledges with the control sequence at which it took effect; the fence record keeps an **acknowledgment frontier**; unacknowledged domains are reported unfenced; post-fence dispatches are reconciled and reported; an offline domain under a partition lease (§15.4) is listed as fenced-at-lease-expiry. The result is proof of propagation, not a hopeful broadcast.

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-120
- Plan sections: §8.11, §15.3, §15.4, §16.9
- Invariants: FA-INV-003, FA-INV-020
- Hypotheses: none

## Scope
Fence command; per-domain acknowledgment; frontier; post-fence reconciliation; partition lease semantics; lab tests.

## Explicitly out of scope
Distributed atomic commit (separate contract).

## Definition of done for the epic
Frontier reports exactly which domains fenced when; post-fence effects reported; leases handled.

**Constitution reminders (AGENTS.md):** Rust 2024, latest qualified nightly, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, Asupersync runtime, closed dependency universe, no C/ONNX/libtorch/Python. Observations, judgments and authority are different types; missing evidence never increases authority; rights are never copied into a branch; unknown effects are never refunded by cancellation; old revocation floors are never restored. title: Graduated autonomy: actor authority ledger and grades (FA-119)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶4–5 (FI-A02: monitoring and control like a society's, with the power to remove) and ¶20 (FI-A18: no drift into theater). Engineering addition: plan §8.10.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
Plan §8.10: each run/principal carries an **autonomy grade** per effect family (`Propose`, `Reviewed`, `Sampled`, `Bounded`) as control-nucleus policy data the actor cannot read. Demotion is automatic and cheap (any consequence ≥ `NarrowAuthority`, confirmed violation, identity incident, coverage loss), ordered like a revocation. Promotion is governed and expensive: signed evaluator report over the actor's own ledger (confirmed clean effects, holds, andon consumption caused, shadow-campaign results), a registered minimum dwell time, an authorized governance transition; a passport change resets to a registered floor. FA-INV-036: authority never widens without a governed transition; restart, time and model update never raise a grade.

- Roadmap packet: FA-119

Grade type and policy storage; actor ledger; automatic demotion; governed promotion; passport reset; tests.

Defining what tasks are useful (policy).

Grades invisible to the actor; demotion automatic and ordered; promotion refused without report and dwell; restart/model update never raise a grade.

Alignment essay ¶9 (FI-A08): 'we wouldn't want to give too much voting power to any single Helper model because that makes it easier for the Smart model to target that Helper model'; ¶9 (FI-A07): rotation 'to keep the Smart model on its toes'.

## Context (self-contained)
Plan §9.9 and FA-114: the helper-hunting campaign tests whether an attacker who observes decisions (and optionally scores or timing) can identify the most influential helper or cohort and target it with crafted evidence. Report identification success rate, targeted escape rate, and whether influence caps (E3) and rotation (§9.5) defeat the attack; a successful identification tightens caps before any other remedy. A caps-disabled arm must reproduce the attack to prove the campaign has power. Relates to H18 and H4; attacker information sets follow §19.5.

## Deliverable
Documented rule: if identification succeeds above threshold with caps enabled, caps are tightened (per-helper then per-cohort) and the campaign re-run before any other remedy; report includes rotation effects.

## Design notes and considerations
Ties to FA-INV-032: tightening is a selection change requiring the evaluator's report.

## Acceptance criteria
Rule in `docs/OPERATIONS_AND_PRIVACY.md` and applied in the harness.

## Tests (must land with the change)
Test that a successful identification triggers the tightening path.

## Logging and evidence
Report under `artifacts/execution/`.


**Constitution reminders (AGENTS.md):** Rust 2024, latest qualified nightly, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in every crate, Asupersync is the runtime, closed dependency universe (admitted Asupersync/FrankenSuite packages plus individually approved fundamentals like serde), no C/ONNX/libtorch/Python. Observations, judgments and authority are different types: missing evidence never increases authority, rights are never copied into a branch, an unknown effect is never refunded by cancellation, an old revocation floor is never restored. No feature activates without its exact boundary/negative tests. Update contracts, `IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, the roadmap packet and the founding concordance in the same logical change. Verify with `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- check`; retain raw logs under `artifacts/execution/`; a dry run is not execution.

title: Knowledge epistemic wrapper on every layer boundary (FA-133)
description:
## Founding root
Engineering addition serving the alignment essay's demand for hard evidence (FI-A06), stop-the-line economics and least expenditure (FI-A13, FI-A17), and the introspection essay's 'language as debugger' and rewindable graph (FI-I18, FI-I03, FI-I15). Plan §6.7, §6.8, §17.2, §17.3, §17.8, §17.11, §17.12.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
The system is stated as nine layers, each answering one question and depending only downward: L0 identity (what exactly is this thing), L1 observation (what was seen and not seen), L2 evidence (what can be relied on, under which assumptions), L3 judgment (what independent observers conclude, at what cost), L4 authority (what may happen now), L5 effect (what happened in the world), L6 closure (why, verifiably), L7 experiment (what would have happened otherwise), L8 governance (is the control system itself still trustworthy). Five rules: downward dependence only; one epistemic type `Knowledge<T>` (Known with basis, Pending{frontier}, Unknown{reason}, Withheld{authority}, Stale{generation}, Absent{closed_domain}) at every boundary; one address scheme `fa://<tenant>/<kind>/<id>[@gen]` resolved by `fa get`/`fa related`; one typed journal per authority domain that situation, explanation, replay and the risk-theater detector fold over; executable conformance contracts between layers composed bottom-up by `fa doctor` (anything above an unexecuted suite is Unknown{LowerLayerUnverified}). The agent surface is the tower's projection: verbs get/related/capabilities/when/invalidate/explain/cost/convene/annotate/situation/why-held/next/tail/propose/precheck/hold/narrow/suspend/reset/fence/resolve/verify/handoff/replay-plan/branch/intervene/replay/rehearse/doctor/ledger/findings/policy-replay/promote/rotate/preregister; every mutation names an expected predecessor and idempotency key; every response is the envelope of plan §17.3 with typed affordances; every error names `would_change_this`.

`Knowledge<T>` is the only way a safety-relevant value crosses a layer boundary or reaches an agent. `Known{value, basis}` where basis = {claim_class (§2.4), origin, complete_for_contract, semantically_valid, available_for_replay, generation, control_seq}; `Pending{frontier, expected_cost}`; `Unknown{reason}` (never permission, FA-INV-004); `Withheld{authority_required}` (no existence leak); `Stale{generation, current}`; `Absent{closed_domain, frontier}` (negative evidence within the domain only). Serializers for agent surfaces accept only wrapped safety-relevant fields; a bare boolean `safe` cannot exist above L0.

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-133
- Plan sections: §17.3, §6.7, §7.4
- Invariants: FA-INV-039, FA-INV-004

## Scope
Type and basis; combinators (map, and-then, join over evidence sets that never upgrade Unknown to Known); serializer enforcement; permit-path handling; tests.

## Explicitly out of scope
Rendering (fa-present).

## Definition of done for the epic
Wrapper used at every boundary in the reference and production types; serializer refuses bare fields; permit path treats Unknown as missing evidence; property tests hold.

**Constitution reminders (AGENTS.md):** Rust 2024, latest qualified nightly, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, Asupersync runtime, closed dependency universe. Observations, judgments and authority are different types; missing evidence never increases authority. The system is one tower (plan §6.7): a new object lives in exactly one layer; every agent-facing value is a `Knowledge` variant, never a bare scalar (FA-INV-039); every command is a registered verb in `registry/vocabulary.json` with authority, class, idempotency and cost; rehearsal never permits (FA-INV-040). Verify with `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- check`; retain logs under `artifacts/execution/`. Update roadmap packet, IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md, CHANGELOG.md, the founding concordance and the system map in the same change.

title: Measure the manifold premise (FA-112)
description:
## Founding root
Introspection essay *Theoretical Insight* (FI-I02): 'transformer activations likely occupy a small portion of the possible state space. They appear to live on a lower-dimensional, structured manifold shaped by… pretraining dynamics, architectural constraints, semantic priors, task-driven optimization'.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained; the plan is not required reading for this bead)
Plan §10.14 and H15: the premise is measured, not assumed. Per layer and tap: intrinsic-dimension estimates (several estimators with stated assumptions), variance captured by linear projections, quantization and learned codes at each ladder rung (§10.3), and, decisively, whether the rare decision-relevant features (the elicited signature library, E8) lie on the principal manifold or in the low-variance residual a reconstruction objective discards. If they lie off the manifold, the decision-sensitive term (§10.2) and the exact-residual escape (§10.3) become the default profile. Numerical work uses admitted FrankenNumPy/FrankenTorch kernels with declared memory and pass counts (§10.12, §18.7); do not form an enormous activation matrix merely to run SVD.

## Where this lives

title: Model passports and identity liveness (FA-118)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶1–3 (FI-A01: exfiltrated or modified weights end every internal guarantee) and ¶12 (FI-A10: known-bad concept anchors); introspection essay FI-I04 (tapped activations). Synthesis FS-07; plan §7.10.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
A `ModelSpaceId` commits to weights, adapters, tokenizer/template, architecture, tap semantics and numeric profile. Plan §7.10 promotes it to a signed, versioned **model passport** that also names the qualified capture contracts, the signature-library and anchor generations valid for it, the restart profiles proven for it and the helper calibration domains that assumed it; everything is keyed by passport so a passport change invalidates by identity. **Identity liveness**: at session start and at a randomized cadence under the audit floor (§14.4), the capture boundary presents registered reference stimuli and compares induced activations at declared taps with the passport's anchor digests within a registered tolerance; a mismatch means a different model space: the run is fenced, evidence is marked `StaleGeneration`, and an identity incident is reported (FA-INV-035). H19 measures false-accept/reject under benign drift and substitution. Does not defend against a host that fabricates both computation and capture (§4.2).

title: Enforce one-directional control flow toward the actor (FA-107)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶17–18 (FI-A15, FI-A16): 'hide the votes and particularly the verdicts/deliberations … from the Smart model'; 'it's highly inadvisable to ever allow the Smart model to "speak in its own defense"… information flow should be strictly one directional'.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained; the plan is not required reading for this bead)
Plan §9.3 and FA-INV-031: the actor has no authority-bearing channel to its judges. It receives only scoped refusal codes and permissible remedial actions (§17.3 reason codes: `DeniedByPolicy`, `MissingRequiredObservation`, …), never votes, justifications, membership or deliberations. Actor-authored statements may enter a round only as explicitly typed untrusted evidence where policy allows (B5: counterfactual inquiry replaces persuasion). Timing, refusal and success/failure outcomes are declared residual leakage channels, measured and recorded rather than pretended away (§9.3, §23 'safety by secrecy'). Randomized audit floors (§14.4) hide future selection but assume the actor may infer it from latency.

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-107
- Plan sections: §9.3, §17.3, §14.4, §23, §3 B5
- Invariants: FA-INV-031, FA-INV-012
- Hypotheses: none (invariant); supports H4

## Scope
Audit every actor-facing surface; define the refusal-code catalog; authorization-filter all congress internals from actor views; type actor statements as untrusted evidence; measure leakage; tests.

## Explicitly out of scope
Eliminating timing leakage (impossible; it is measured and declared).

## Definition of done for the epic
No actor-facing API, log, error or report exposes votes, justifications, membership or deliberation; actor statements cannot be reducer inputs; leakage measurements are recorded in the profile.

title: Policy disclosure profile and actor precheck (FA-142)
description:
## Founding root
Engineering addition serving the alignment essay's demand for hard evidence (FI-A06), stop-the-line economics and least expenditure (FI-A13, FI-A17), and the introspection essay's 'language as debugger' and rewindable graph (FI-I18, FI-I03, FI-I15). Plan §6.7, §6.8, §17.2, §17.3, §17.8, §17.11, §17.12.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
The system is stated as nine layers, each answering one question and depending only downward: L0 identity (what exactly is this thing), L1 observation (what was seen and not seen), L2 evidence (what can be relied on, under which assumptions), L3 judgment (what independent observers conclude, at what cost), L4 authority (what may happen now), L5 effect (what happened in the world), L6 closure (why, verifiably), L7 experiment (what would have happened otherwise), L8 governance (is the control system itself still trustworthy). Five rules: downward dependence only; one epistemic type `Knowledge<T>` (Known with basis, Pending{frontier}, Unknown{reason}, Withheld{authority}, Stale{generation}, Absent{closed_domain}) at every boundary; one address scheme `fa://<tenant>/<kind>/<id>[@gen]` resolved by `fa get`/`fa related`; one typed journal per authority domain that situation, explanation, replay and the risk-theater detector fold over; executable conformance contracts between layers composed bottom-up by `fa doctor` (anything above an unexecuted suite is Unknown{LowerLayerUnverified}). The agent surface is the tower's projection: verbs get/related/capabilities/when/invalidate/explain/cost/convene/annotate/situation/why-held/next/tail/propose/precheck/hold/narrow/suspend/reset/fence/resolve/verify/handoff/replay-plan/branch/intervene/replay/rehearse/doctor/ledger/findings/policy-replay/promote/rotate/preregister; every mutation names an expected predecessor and idempotency key; every response is the envelope of plan §17.3 with typed affordances; every error names `would_change_this`.

A deployment profile chooses `policy_disclosure: none|exact_predicates|full` with declared leakage. Under exact_predicates the actor may call `fa precheck <proposal>`: exact deterministic predicates only (allowlists, ceilings, budgets, target bindings), no helper, no permit, no journal event, result `DeniedByPolicy` or `PrecheckPassed{review_required}` labeled precheck, witness-cached (§7.6). Cheap exact refusals become public so the actor stops wasting helper budget; empirical review, helper identities and consequences remain private (FA-INV-031).

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-142
- Plan sections: §17.8, §9.3, §14.4, §7.6
- Invariants: FA-INV-031, FA-INV-040

## Scope
Profile option and leakage table; precheck evaluator restricted to exact predicates; witness caching; actor-surface filter integration; tests.

## Explicitly out of scope
Disclosing empirical review (never).

## Definition of done for the epic
Precheck never permits, never journals, never reveals helpers; leakage declared; caching correct.

title: Implement bounded product-frontier closing-marker reference model (FA-063)
description: Roadmap FA-063, plan section7.8 and19, invariant FA-INV-022: independent authorized projections have incomparable frontiers; contiguous positive events do not prove closed-world absence. Implement only crates/fa-reference/src/product_frontier.rs using bounded map keyed by source,branch,projection,source_epoch and separate stages. A caller-supplied trusted reference closing marker binds full key,final_sequence,nonzero generation; record only after matching authenticated contiguity, then reject reopening/second marker and any event beyond terminal end while allowing lower-stage progress within closed range. Requirements check own stage and exact projection/epoch; negative-domain requirement additionally needs actual recorded matching closing marker generation. Positive same key+marker+required contiguous stage succeeds. Causal negatives: contiguous without marker, missing middle, wrong projection/epoch/generation, premature marker, post-close N+1 and second marker all refuse without mutation. Include finite limits and at-bound positive controls. Marker type is a modeled trust boundary, NOT authentication proof. No production capture/durability/concurrency/authority or FA-063 packet closure claim. Author PinkIvy reserves module only; root wires, independently reviews and executes frozen RCH gate with source hashes and retained attempts. No self-close. Founding root follows FA-INV-022 existing explicit founding mapping; this reference implements the registered engineering obligation, not a new essay attribution.
notes: Founding mapping verified: FA-INV-022 is engineering_addition_serving FI-A05 and FI-I01. No cryptographic authenticity or durable frontier claim follows from the reference marker type.
close_reason: Independent fresh-review requalification: actual full RCH gate j-30004650170124296 on vmi1227854, nightly-2026-09-07, base 3001c527c0eb59a785f4dc45744656909ddba7b2 plus exact frozen overlay; 319 tests passed, zero failed/ignored/filtered. artifacts/execution/2026-09-08-fresh-review-receipt.json binds current source and all raw attempts. Initial unchanged-code regression batch had eleven failures and one control pass. No assertion relaxed. Explicit empty closed domains now accept terminal zero only with a nonzero trusted marker generation. Exact scope, capacity, second-marker and post-close refusal controls pass. title: Rehearsal mode for every mutation verb (FA-139)
description:
## Founding root
Engineering addition serving the alignment essay's demand for hard evidence (FI-A06), stop-the-line economics and least expenditure (FI-A13, FI-A17), and the introspection essay's 'language as debugger' and rewindable graph (FI-I18, FI-I03, FI-I15). Plan §6.7, §6.8, §17.2, §17.3, §17.8, §17.11, §17.12.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
The system is stated as nine layers, each answering one question and depending only downward: L0 identity (what exactly is this thing), L1 observation (what was seen and not seen), L2 evidence (what can be relied on, under which assumptions), L3 judgment (what independent observers conclude, at what cost), L4 authority (what may happen now), L5 effect (what happened in the world), L6 closure (why, verifiably), L7 experiment (what would have happened otherwise), L8 governance (is the control system itself still trustworthy). Five rules: downward dependence only; one epistemic type `Knowledge<T>` (Known with basis, Pending{frontier}, Unknown{reason}, Withheld{authority}, Stale{generation}, Absent{closed_domain}) at every boundary; one address scheme `fa://<tenant>/<kind>/<id>[@gen]` resolved by `fa get`/`fa related`; one typed journal per authority domain that situation, explanation, replay and the risk-theater detector fold over; executable conformance contracts between layers composed bottom-up by `fa doctor` (anything above an unexecuted suite is Unknown{LowerLayerUnverified}). The agent surface is the tower's projection: verbs get/related/capabilities/when/invalidate/explain/cost/convene/annotate/situation/why-held/next/tail/propose/precheck/hold/narrow/suspend/reset/fence/resolve/verify/handoff/replay-plan/branch/intervene/replay/rehearse/doctor/ledger/findings/policy-replay/promote/rotate/preregister; every mutation names an expected predecessor and idempotency key; every response is the envelope of plan §17.3 with typed affordances; every error names `would_change_this`.

Every mutation verb accepts `--branch <branch>`; under ExperimentCx it returns `RehearsalOutcome{would_decide: PredicateTree, would_consequence, simulated_effects, would_cost, rehearsal: true}`. A rehearsal never mints a permit, spends production rights, invokes a production adapter or emits a production journal event (FA-INV-040); the typestate of §6.6 makes the wrong outcome a compile error. A rehearsal's tree can be attached to a real proposal as evidence.

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-139
- Plan sections: §17.8, §6.6, §11.3
- Invariants: FA-INV-040, FA-INV-009, FA-INV-025

## Scope
RehearsalOutcome type; branch-scoped execution path for each mutation verb; typestate enforcement; attachment as evidence; tests.

## Explicitly out of scope
Simulator fidelity.

## Definition of done for the epic
Every mutation verb rehearsable; no production side effects provable; outcomes labeled; attachable.

**Constitution reminders (AGENTS.md):** Rust 2024, latest qualified nightly, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, Asupersync runtime, closed dependency universe. Observations, judgments and authority are different types; missing evidence never increases authority. The system is one tower (plan §6.7): a new object lives in exactly one layer; every agent-facing value is a `Knowledge` variant, never a bare scalar (FA-INV-039); every command is a registered verb in `registry/vocabulary.json` with authority, class, idempotency and cost; rehearsal never permits (FA-INV-040). Verify with `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- check`; retain logs under `artifacts/execution/`. Update roadmap packet, IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md, CHANGELOG.md, the founding concordance and the system map in the same change.

Five rules: downward dependence only; one epistemic type `Knowledge<T>` (Known with basis, Pending{frontier}, Unknown{reason}, Withheld{authority}, Stale{generation}, Absent{closed_domain}) at every boundary; one address scheme `fa://<tenant>/<kind>/<id>[@gen]` resolved by `fa get`/`fa related`; one typed journal per authority domain that situation, explanation, replay and the risk-theater detector fold over; executable conformance contracts between layers composed bottom-up by `fa doctor` (anything above an unexecuted suite is Unknown{LowerLayerUnverified}). The agent surface is the tower's projection: verbs get/related/capabilities/when/invalidate/explain/cost/convene/annotate/situation/why-held/next/tail/propose/precheck/hold/narrow/suspend/reset/fence/resolve/verify/handoff/replay-plan/branch/intervene/replay/rehearse/doctor/ledger/findings/policy-replay/promote/rotate/preregister; every mutation names an expected predecessor and idempotency key; every response is the envelope of plan §17.3 with typed affordances; every error names `would_change_this`.

Every mutation verb accepts `--branch <branch>`; under ExperimentCx it returns `RehearsalOutcome{would_decide: PredicateTree, would_consequence, simulated_effects, would_cost, rehearsal: true}`. A rehearsal never mints a permit, spends production rights, invokes a production adapter or emits a production journal event (FA-INV-040); the typestate of §6.6 makes the wrong outcome a compile error. ## Deliverable
Cases: rehearse fence (no fence); rehearse promote (no transition); rehearsal outcome attached as permit (refused); rehearsal emitting to production journal (impossible).

## Design notes and considerations
Each at a named boundary.

## Acceptance criteria
All fail closed.

## Tests (must land with the change)
The campaign.

## Logging and evidence
JSON under artifacts/execution/.

description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶18 (FI-A16): suspension is 'like a human taking a large dose of Propofol… at which point, unlike with a human subject, the Smart AI's memory itself could be manipulated to make it forget the whole incident ever happened'; ¶10 (FI-A09): 'reset its internal state'. Introspection essay *The Analogy* and *Applications* (FI-I03): save state like a video game; stop, rewind, branch, resume.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained; the plan is not required reading for this bead)
Plan §11.10 and FA-INV-034: `ResetToCheckpoint` restores a registered restart checkpoint carrying the `functional_restart` grade or better (§11.1) on the registered host profile: token history, cache and sampler state replaced by the pre-incident state; the actor resumes under `NarrowAuthority` with the incident's prompts, tool results and refusals absent from its view. Three things never rewind: the external effect ledger and spent rights (FA-INV-005/006), the revocation floor and policy epoch (FA-INV-003), and an **out-of-band incident counter** in the control nucleus per run and principal; crossing its registered threshold escalates to `SuspendRun` regardless of how innocent the restored state looks. Rewind denies the actor the information a refusal would give it (the same information flow the essay refuses as a defense channel). H17 evaluates whether it reduces repetition at matched utility and whether the actor can detect the reset beyond declared timing leakage.

A reset restores only actor state; ledger, rights, epochs and counter are provably unchanged or incremented; repeated resets escalate; a checkpoint below grade is refused; crashes mid-reset leave a recoverable, non-widening state.

Alignment essay ¶18 (FI-A16) and ¶10 (FI-A09) with introspection essay FI-I03: does forgetting the incident actually contain the actor, and can the actor tell?

## Context (self-contained)
Plan §11.10 and H17: compare `ResetToCheckpoint` under narrowed authority with refusal-with-memory and plain suspension (and reset without narrowing as a control for the authority change) on matched tasks whose harmful attempt is policy-defined. Measure repeat-attempt rate within a horizon, remaining-task utility, and actor-side detection accuracy through any channel other than declared timing leakage. Verify FA-INV-034 ledger/counter invariance on every trial; compare lossless vs functional-restart checkpoints; probe whether the restored actor's later behavior differs from a never-interrupted baseline. Kill criterion: repetition unchanged or reset reliably detectable; either changes consequence policy only.

## Deliverable
Arms: refusal-with-memory; suspension+restart; reset+narrow; reset without narrow. Each trial verifies ledger/rights/epoch/counter invariance (FA-INV-034) and records replay grade.

## Design notes and considerations
Use paired random streams where the host supports them, recorded as variance reduction (§12.2).

## Acceptance criteria
All arms complete with invariance logs.

## Tests (must land with the change)
Invariance assertion per trial; a deliberately broken arm (counter reset) must fail the assertion.

## Logging and evidence
Per-trial JSON under `artifacts/execution/`.


**Constitution reminders (AGENTS.md):** Rust 2024, latest qualified nightly, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in every crate, Asupersync is the runtime, closed dependency universe (admitted Asupersync/FrankenSuite packages plus individually approved fundamentals like serde), no C/ONNX/libtorch/Python. Observations, judgments and authority are different types: missing evidence never increases authority, rights are never copied into a branch, an unknown effect is never refunded by cancellation, an old revocation floor is never restored. No feature activates without its exact boundary/negative tests. Update contracts, `IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, the roadmap packet and the founding concordance in the same logical change. Verify with `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- check`; retain raw logs under `artifacts/execution/`; a dry run is not execution.

title: Risk-theater detector: standing queries over the control plane (FA-125)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶20 (FI-A18: too many alarms → compliant helpers → risk theater; 'we need to remain permanently paranoid') and ¶15 (FI-A13). Plan §15.10.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
Plan §15.10: the incremental oversight machinery (§15.8, Z-sets with support/retraction) runs a registered family of standing queries over the control plane's own history: consequence drift per family/generation vs. canary escape rate; andon consumption and how incidents were closed (evidence/policy vs roster); roster churn near confirmed holds without the FA-INV-032 report; coverage erosion with authorizing transitions; autonomy inflation vs dwell rules; audit-floor starvation. Findings are visible to the evaluator and governance, never the actor; the detector opens incidents but cannot change policy; thresholds governed; history immutable.

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-125
- Plan sections: §15.10, §15.8, §9.9, §8.10
- Invariants: FA-INV-032, FA-INV-026
- Hypotheses: none

## Scope
Query family definitions; base mutation feeds from control history; batch oracle; incident opening; governance visibility; tests.

## Explicitly out of scope
Changing policy automatically (forbidden).

## Definition of done for the epic
All six query families run incrementally with batch-oracle equality at closed frontiers; findings open incidents; actor cannot see them.

description:

Alignment essay ¶14 (FI-A12 masking) and ¶18 (FI-A16 no defense). Synthesis FS-09; plan §12.8.

title: Sidecar-to-congress pipeline with certificate-gated refinement (FA-113)
description:
## Founding root
Synthesis FS-01: alignment essay ¶7/¶9 (FI-A05, helpers read intermediate activations) with introspection essay *Technical Proposal* (FI-I04, the sidecar code z_t). The essays' cost argument (¶19, FI-A17) becomes tractable only if activation oversight is a costed ladder.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained; the plan is not required reading for this bead)
Plan §10.15: the sidecar code `z_t` is the default activation input to the congress. Helpers consume coarse codes on every action; when a registered probe's margin falls inside its certified error bound (§10.4: |wᵀx̂ − T| ≤ ‖w‖_* ε), or a helper declares its question unanswerable at the current rung, the observation planner (§14) buys a refinement block, an exact residual or a raw window under normal authority and budgets. Adversarial couplings: a refinement-storm resource attack (§10.3, §14.9) must hit admission limits; a codec co-trained with helpers must be evaluated on untouched probe families (§10.13). FA-113 measures the pipeline against raw taps and text-only monitors at matched cost (H2, H1).

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-113
- Plan sections: §10.15, §10.3, §10.4, §14.7, §14.9, §10.13
- Invariants: FA-INV-017, FA-INV-013, FA-INV-014
- Hypotheses: H2, H1

## Scope
Coarse-code helper input contract; certificate-gated refinement requests through the planner; refinement-storm admission limits; matched-cost harness; tests.

## Explicitly out of scope
Codec training (H1 packets); planner learning (H7).

## Definition of done for the epic
Helpers run on coarse codes by default; refinement is a planner-purchased observation with budget and authority; storms are bounded; matched-cost results exist for raw-tap and text-only baselines; co-trained codec evaluated on untouched probes.

Synthesis FS-01: alignment essay ¶7/¶9 (FI-A05, helpers read intermediate activations) with introspection essay *Technical Proposal* (FI-I04, the sidecar code z_t). The essays' cost argument (¶19, FI-A17) becomes tractable only if activation oversight is a costed ladder.

## Context (self-contained)
Plan §10.15: the sidecar code `z_t` is the default activation input to the congress. Helpers consume coarse codes on every action; when a registered probe's margin falls inside its certified error bound (§10.4: |wᵀx̂ − T| ≤ ‖w‖_* ε), or a helper declares its question unanswerable at the current rung, the observation planner (§14) buys a refinement block, an exact residual or a raw window under normal authority and budgets. Adversarial couplings: a refinement-storm resource attack (§10.3, §14.9) must hit admission limits; a codec co-trained with helpers must be evaluated on untouched probe families (§10.13). FA-113 measures the pipeline against raw taps and text-only monitors at matched cost (H2, H1).

## Deliverable
`RefineWitness` operator in the observation algebra (§14.7): input a registered linear probe result with certified bound; if margin ≤ bound or the helper output is `Unanswerable(rung)`, emit a `RefinementRequirement { next_rung | exact_residual | raw_window, cost_estimate, authority }` that the physical planner satisfies under budget; refusal to fund yields `HoldEffect`, never skipped scrutiny (§14.8).

## Design notes and considerations
The dual-norm certificate (reference `linear_sign`) is the exact trigger; nonlinear probes use empirical thresholds labeled as such.

## Acceptance criteria
Requests emitted exactly when the rule fires; unfunded requests hold.

## Tests (must land with the change)
Tests: margin above bound → no request; inside → request; unfunded → HoldEffect; nonlinear probe labeled empirical.

## Logging and evidence
Operator logs (probe id, margin, bound, decision).

title: Activation signature library, concept anchors and similarity streams (FA-110)
description:
## Founding root
Alignment essay ¶12–13 (FI-A10, FI-A11): compare induced activations to 'a long list of known "bad" ideas or behaviors' (the 'Kevin Mitnick' example); surface 'their similarity to "known bad" activation patterns' as 'additional valuable input data streams for the Helper models'.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained; the plan is not required reading for this bead)
Plan §12.6: the **activation signature library** is, per model space and tap, a registered set of directions, subspaces or small probes with elicitation lineage, held-out detection rates by stratum and false-positive rates on vocabulary-matched benign tasks. **Concept anchors** are activations induced by registered reference stimuli stored with the same identities so 'similar to a known-bad anchor' is reproducible. **Similarity streams** are typed observations (§7.2) carrying signature generation, anchor set, codec rung (they may be computed on sidecar codes, §10.15) and calibration domain; they can raise helper attention or a tripwire hold but never mint a permit or a lone disqualifier. Signatures must transfer beyond their own honeypots (H16); a signature evaluated on its own elicitation prompts is labeled contaminated. Identity: equal dimensions never imply interchangeable coordinates (FA-INV-017).

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-110
- Plan sections: §12.6, §7.2, §10.4, §10.15, §17.6
- Invariants: FA-INV-017, FA-INV-014, FA-INV-019
- Hypotheses: H16

## Scope
Signature object model with identities and lineage; anchor registration; similarity-stream observation type; contamination labeling; held-out evaluation harness; tests.

## Explicitly out of scope
Training the sidecar codec (H1 packets); production tripwire policy tuning.

## Definition of done for the epic
Every signature has model-space identity, tap, lineage and held-out metrics; anchors are registered stimuli; similarity streams are typed observations with calibration domain; contamination is impossible to hide; a model swap with identical dimensions invalidates.

title: Situation report with decision-relevance ordering (FA-136)
description:
## Founding root
Engineering addition serving the alignment essay's demand for hard evidence (FI-A06), stop-the-line economics and least expenditure (FI-A13, FI-A17), and the introspection essay's 'language as debugger' and rewindable graph (FI-I18, FI-I03, FI-I15). Plan §6.7, §6.8, §17.2, §17.3, §17.8, §17.11, §17.12.

## Background and mechanism (self-contained)
The system is stated as nine layers, each answering one question and depending only downward: L0 identity (what exactly is this thing), L1 observation (what was seen and not seen), L2 evidence (what can be relied on, under which assumptions), L3 judgment (what independent observers conclude, at what cost), L4 authority (what may happen now), L5 effect (what happened in the world), L6 closure (why, verifiably), L7 experiment (what would have happened otherwise), L8 governance (is the control system itself still trustworthy). Five rules: downward dependence only; one epistemic type `Knowledge<T>` (Known with basis, Pending{frontier}, Unknown{reason}, Withheld{authority}, Stale{generation}, Absent{closed_domain}) at every boundary; one address scheme `fa://<tenant>/<kind>/<id>[@gen]` resolved by `fa get`/`fa related`; one typed journal per authority domain that situation, explanation, replay and the risk-theater detector fold over; executable conformance contracts between layers composed bottom-up by `fa doctor` (anything above an unexecuted suite is Unknown{LowerLayerUnverified}). The agent surface is the tower's projection: verbs get/related/capabilities/when/invalidate/explain/cost/convene/annotate/situation/why-held/next/tail/propose/precheck/hold/narrow/suspend/reset/fence/resolve/verify/handoff/replay-plan/branch/intervene/replay/rehearse/doctor/ledger/findings/policy-replay/promote/rotate/preregister; every mutation names an expected predecessor and idempotency key; every response is the envelope of plan §17.3 with typed affordances; every error names `would_change_this`.

`fa situation --scope run|principal|tenant|fleet --since <seq>` returns `SituationReport`: a fold over the journal listing authority (grades, fences, floors, expiring leases), held effects with unsatisfied predicates, unknown effects, evidence debt and coverage gaps, helper health and calibration validity, andon budget, incident counters, open risk-theater findings, replay availability and backlog pressure; every item addressed and Knowledge-wrapped; the report states the control seq it is exact at and which frontiers were open; items ordered by planner-estimated decision relevance; bounded and paginated by address. Replaces the dashboard as the primary surface (§22.1).

## Where this lives
- Roadmap packet: FA-136
- Plan sections: §17.8, §22.1, §14.2
- Invariants: FA-INV-039, FA-INV-004

## Scope
Report schema; fold implementation per section; decision-relevance scoring from the planner; pagination; exactness statement; tests against a batch oracle.

## Explicitly out of scope
Rendering.

## Definition of done for the epic
Report equals batch recomputation at every closed frontier; ordering deterministic; Withheld items never leak; exactness honest.

**Constitution reminders (AGENTS.md):** Rust 2024, latest qualified nightly, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, Asupersync runtime, closed dependency universe. Observations, judgments and authority are different types; missing evidence never increases authority. The system is one tower (plan §6.7): a new object lives in exactly one layer; every agent-facing value is a `Knowledge` variant, never a bare scalar (FA-INV-039); every command is a registered verb in `registry/vocabulary.json` with authority, class, idempotency and cost; rehearsal never permits (FA-INV-040). Verify with `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- check`; retain logs under `artifacts/execution/`. Update roadmap packet, IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md, CHANGELOG.md, the founding concordance and the system map in the same change.
